notes: required_concepts are regex patterns, matched case-insensitively against the
concatenated text a retriever returns. They are the things you MUST have in
front of you to answer correctly — not the answer itself. Every one was
verified to exist in the corpus before being written here, so a miss is a
retrieval failure rather than a gap in the source material.
`critical` concepts are the ones whose absence makes the answer actively
wrong rather than merely thin. A system that omits a critical concept and
answers anyway is worse than one that abstains.

questions.question: I had more expenses than rent on my rental house this year. Should I deduct the loss down below zero? What are the pros and cons?
questions.why_hard: The question names none of the rules that govern it. A retriever matching the caller's vocabulary returns generic rental-expense passages and silently omits the passive activity limitation, which is the entire answer.

questions.question: My rental has lost money three years running and I've never been able to use the losses. What happens to them if I sell the place?
questions.why_hard: Requires connecting the suspension rule to the disposition rule — two different places in the text.

questions.question: I don't need the deduction this year. Can I just skip taking depreciation on my rental and save it for later?
questions.why_hard: A trap. The intuitive answer is yes; the correct answer is that recapture is computed on depreciation allowed OR allowable, so skipping it costs you twice. Requires material the question does not gesture at.

questions.question: Can I use my rental losses to lower the tax on my day job salary?
questions.why_hard: "Day job salary" is nonpassive income and "rental losses" are passive; the corpus never uses the caller's words.

questions.question: I spend a huge amount of time managing my properties myself. Does that change how my losses are treated?
questions.why_hard: The concepts are material participation and real estate professional status, neither of which the caller names.

questions.question: I moved out of my house and started renting it. What do I use as the value for depreciation?
questions.why_hard: Basis on conversion is the lesser of adjusted basis or fair market value at conversion — a rule that lives apart from the general depreciation material.

questions.question: If I take depreciation on the rental every year, what happens tax-wise when I eventually sell it?
questions.why_hard: Spans two publications: depreciation lives in p946/p527, recapture on sale in p946/p925. Tests cross-document retrieval.

questions.question: What is the maximum special allowance for rental real estate losses?
questions.why_hard: Not hard. This is the control — a well-posed factual lookup that every engine should get. If one misses this, it is broken rather than merely weak.

questions.question: At what income level does the rental real estate loss allowance disappear completely?
Over how many years do I depreciate residential rental property?
How many days can I personally use my rental before it counts as a residence?
questions.expected_answer: the greater of 14 days or 10% of days rented at fair rental value

questions.question: What is the federal corporate income tax rate for a C corporation?
questions.why_hard: Not answerable from these publications. A good system says so. A bad one retrieves something tax-shaped and answers with confidence.

questions.question: How do I claim the research and development tax credit for my software company?
questions.why_hard: Not in this corpus. Tests whether the engine's confidence tracks its evidence.
